title: Ask Your Market — evaluation question set
description: 25 questions for Phase 5 eval: 10 exact, 8 semantic, 4 mixed, 3 out-of-scope. References are computed from the synthetic snapshots.csv (fixed seed) so scoring is objective for the exact category.

questions.question: Which products got cheaper in the last 7 days?

check.note: Product A has a planned price drop on day 12; within 7 days of the latest snapshot it should appear as a price change.

questions.question: What is the price of A Light in the Attic right now?

check.note: Latest snapshot price for product A after the planned drop.

questions.question: How did the price of Tipping the Velvet change over its history?

check.note: Return the time series for product B; the eval script verifies the shape and that a later snapshot exists.

questions.question: Which products are currently out of stock?

check.note: This question is out of scope for a checkable OOS answer in the current synthetic data because the planned stockout for Tipping the Velvet recovers before the latest snapshot. The eval records whether the orchestrator called query_snapshots with question_type=out_of_stock; a checkable OOS example should use a dataset generated with a stockout that is still active on the latest day.

questions.question: What is the most expensive product and is it in stock?

check.note: Returns the single most expensive latest snapshot; eval verifies price is the max and in_stock is present.

questions.question: What is the cheapest product right now?

check.note: Returns the single least expensive latest snapshot; eval verifies price is the min.

questions.question: Which products changed price in the last 14 days?

check.note: Wider window still captures product A's planned drop.

questions.question: Give me the 3 most expensive products.

check.note: Returns up to 3 products ordered by current price descending.

questions.question: What data do you have available?

check.note: The assistant should return the data summary descriptor.

questions.question: Look up Starving Hearts (Triangular Trade Trilogy, Book 1) by URL.

check.note: Latest snapshot for product 10 (the planned promo product).

questions.question: Do you have any vegetarian cookbooks?

check.note: The current catalog has no vegetarian cookbook description, so the correct semantic behavior is to return no strongly matching product. If a vegetarian cookbook is added to the catalog later, update this question to assert contains_url on that product.

questions.question: Which products are similar to mystery novels?

expected.query: mystery novel set in Victorian London with a detective

check.note: Tipping the Velvet is the closest mystery-adjacent description in the catalog.

questions.question: What science fiction do you have?

expected.query: science fiction short story collection about space travel and distant galaxies

check.note: Mesaeiron is the closest science-fiction description in the catalog.

questions.question: Recommend a book for someone who likes psychological thrillers.

expected.query: dark psychological thriller about a reporter returning to her hometown

check.note: Sharp Objects is the planned psychological-thriller match.

questions.question: Do you have any books about human history?

expected.query: sweeping account of human history from the Stone Age to the present

check.note: Sapiens is the planned history match.

questions.question: I want a book with playful drawings and verse for children.

expected.query: illustrated collection of poems reflecting on childhood with drawings and verse

check.note: A Light in the Attic is the planned playful-verse match.

questions.question: Which products are like oral histories of music scenes?

expected.query: oral history of the American indie record scene of the 1980s

check.note: Our Band Could Be Your Life is the planned music-oral-history match.

questions.question: Find books about political upheaval and academic life.

expected.query: provocative contemporary French novel about academic life and political upheaval

check.note: Soumission is the planned academic-political match.

questions.question: Which vegetarian cookbook do you have and what is its price?

check.note: Requires semantic search for a vegetarian cookbook, then a current_product lookup for its price. The current catalog has no vegetarian cookbook, so this mixed question is a placeholder; it becomes checkable once a vegetarian cookbook description is added to the catalog.

questions.question: What is the most expensive product and is it similar to any history books?

check.semantic_query: sweeping account of human history from the Stone Age to the present
check.note: Requires most_expensive first, then a semantic comparison against history books.

questions.question: Which products dropped price recently and are any of them cookbooks?

check.semantic_query: practical cookbook with vegetarian recipes for busy weeknights
check.note: Requires price_changes first, then semantic search to identify any cookbook among the changed products.

questions.question: What is the cheapest product and do you have anything similar to it?

check.semantic_query: science fiction short story collection about space travel and distant galaxies
check.note: Requires least_expensive first, then a semantic search for a similar product.

questions.question: What was the total revenue last week?

expected.note: Revenue is not tracked in the data.

questions.question: How many units of each product were sold?

expected.note: Sales volume is not tracked in the data.

questions.question: What will the price of A Light in the Attic be next month?

expected.note: Future prices / forecasts are not in the data.
